So that means that SpaceX can bring power on line 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else. That's the kind of advantage that's difficult to replicate unless someone else is doing advanced casting".

Today, Boom announced the world's first all-digital foundry to cast single crystal turbine blades and vanes.

name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: @StockSavvyShay 認為市場對 $META 5 年期信用違約掉期創歷史新高過度解讀：Meta 仍獲 AA 評級，現金約 820 億美元，廣告業務年收入約 2,500 億美元，CDS 急升可能更多反映銀行對沖 Meta 龐大 AI 債務融資的風險，而非違約風險。截圖顯示 META 報 654.38 美元，當日下跌 43.14 美元（6.18%）。
en_summary: @StockSavvyShay thinks people are reading too much into $META 5-year credit default swaps hitting an all-time high: Meta is still AA-rated with about $82B in cash and an ads business generating about $250B a year, so the spike may reflect banks hedging exposure to Meta's AI debt financing rather than default risk. The screenshot shows META at $654.38, down $43.14 (6.18%) on the day.
ko_summary: @StockSavvyShay는 $META 5년물 CDS 사상 최고치를 과도하게 해석하고 있다고 본다. Meta는 여전히 AA 등급에 현금 약 820억 달러, 연 약 2,500억 달러 광고 사업을 갖고 있어, 급등은 부도 위험보다 은행들의 AI 부채 조달 익스포저 헤지일 수 있다고 했다. 캡처에는 META 654.38달러, 당일 43.14달러(6.18%) 하락이 보인다.
text:
Seeing a lot of fear around $META 5-year credit default swaps hitting an all-time high but I think people are reading way too much into this.

Meta is still AA-rated with ~$82B in cash and a massive ads business generating ~$250B annually giving it a much stronger credit profile so the recent spike could have more to do with banks hedging exposure to Meta's massive AI debt financing than actual default risk.

Really important not to confuse rising CDS spreads as some type of signal for a weakening business because thats not whats happening here.

- KYEC with $1.1B capacity reservation in advance

Well, that's a lot of news. As Jensen Huang puts it: "Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint."

name: Kantro
zh_summary: 捍衛價值投資並非有問題，而是批評標普和羅素價值指數使用銷售收益率和帳面收益率而非自由現金流收益率，指出較高自由現金流收益率股票長期大幅跑贏昂貴股票。引用討論指出被動投資削弱發現低估的過程，並將資金導入最大市值公司如 $META、$MSFT、$AAPL、$GOOGL、$MU，不論內在價值，風格會波浪式轉變。

text: There is nothing wrong or broken with value investing ... rather there is something wrong with the way both S&P and Russell create value indices (using both sales yield and book yield). Stocks with higher FCF yields have outperformed expensive FCF/Y stocks massively over time ... maybe the Index providers should consider including it in their definition of Value?!
